Federal Spending Atlas

About the data

Payments and obligations

Payments are reported award outlays. The “All reported payments” view sums USAspending’s total_outlays for indexed prime grants (types 02–05) and contracts (A–D), by place of performance, without an award-date filter. These are cumulative reported payments, not payments made during a selected fiscal year or Congress. They are a reporting snapshot, not every federal payment.

Obligations use transaction-level federal commitments, including negative adjustments, within the selected dates. Loans, direct payments, subawards, federal salaries, and other award types are outside both measures.

Annual and cycle payments use fiscal-year-to-date File C financial reports. Period-end snapshots are counted once. Calendar cycles subtract their opening fiscal quarter and add their closing fiscal quarter. Payment reporting before FY2022 was optional. The 2017–2018 payment cycle is unavailable because FY2017’s opening-quarter report did not exist; combined payments cover the four measurable cycles from 2019. Financial records that cannot be linked to a grant or contract are excluded.

Congressional reporting cycles

The five cycle views use the calendar years corresponding to the 115th–119th Congresses: 2017–2018, 2019–2020, 2021–2022, 2023–2024, and 2025–2026. Reporting cycles begin January 1 and end December 31; they are not exact January 3 swearing-in boundaries. The current cycle ends September 30, 2026 in this snapshot. The combined view adds the five disjoint ranges once. Cycle totals are nominal dollars and are not annualized.

Geography and unallocated amounts

The API aggregates using its derived current congressional-district identifiers, not the districts originally submitted. The map uses Census 2025 cartographic boundaries for the 119th Congress, including 435 voting districts and 6 delegate/resident-commissioner areas. Historical data are presented against those identifiers; this is not an original-year district comparison. Redistricting and geocoding updates can change historical assignments.

Only API identifiers that join to those 441 boundary features enter the mapped totals and rankings. Unknown, multiple-district, and unmatched rows are excluded and retained in the download and raw evidence; excluded totals describe only rows returned by this endpoint, not all unmappable federal spending.

Per-resident comparisons

Per-resident amounts divide the selected amount by the district population returned by USAspending. These are API-supplied reference populations, not annual population estimates or inflation-adjusted amounts. A missing or zero population produces an unavailable value. Population vintage is not specified in the API response. Large institutions and regional awards can dominate a district without representing benefits exclusive to its residents.

Earmarks and sponsorship

The separate GAO compilation covers enacted Community Project Funding and Congressionally Directed Spending for FY2022–FY2024. A project is counted once by GAO ID, including joint House/Senate requests. Requester names are shown as recorded; a requester is not a project location. State totals include only projects with a single state location. Multi-location projects remain separate. Project district totals require further location research.

Congress designated no new CPF/CDS funds in FY2025 according to GAO. That does not mean payments on earlier projects stopped. FY2026 enacted tables, CAGW’s broader pork classification, historical TCS sponsorship files, and POPVOX requests are not merged into the official series here.

Official sources

  • USAspending public API and geography endpoint contract
  • USAspending Federal Spending Guide
  • Census 119th Congress boundary ZIP
  • GAO Tracking the Funds and official compilation ZIP
  • House FY2026 enacted appropriations
  • CAGW earmark database, Taxpayers for Common Sense historical files, POPVOX Appropriations Explorer (context only)

Freshness and reproduction

Map data are saved snapshots. Agency and program details load on request from the public API and may reflect later revisions; their retrieval time is shown separately. No automatic update schedule is enabled. Raw responses and refresh scripts are included in the local project.
